E035-01.notes: Singular possessive with 'a': 'a week's wait'. B (plural possessive) clashes with 'a'; A lacks apostrophe; D is nonstandard. Fact check: stagecoach ~3+ weeks vs ~10 days saves over a week; consistent.

E035-02.notes: Subject is singular 'Each rider'; 'along with' phrase does not make it plural. 'was expected'. C/D plural/tense errors.

E035-03.notes: Compound predicate 'swapped ... and rode on' with one subject takes no comma. B semicolon and C colon require independent clause after. A adds an unneeded comma.

E035-04.notes: Only C conveys speed concretely; 'by some accounts' hedges the commonly cited two-minute figure appropriately. Also fixes the illogical 'so each change took some time'.

E035-05.notes: Parallelism with 'both brave and light'. C infinitive and D clause not parallel with adjective 'brave'; A wordy/nonparallel.

flags: minor: Fort Kearny/Fort Churchill were in Nebraska and Nevada Territories in March 1861 (Nevada not a state until 1864); 'Nebraska and Nevada' is acceptable shorthand
E035-07.notes: The detail illustrates the speed ('remarkable feats'). Fact check: March 1861 inaugural carried telegraph-end to telegraph-end in ~7 days 17 hours; 'under eight days' accurate.

E035-08.notes: Paragraph shifts from feats/speed to finances at 'Despite such feats', a contrast transition. A already begins the paragraph; B and C continue the speed topic.

E035-09.notes: Past tense to match narrative and 'would close'. Fact check: telegraph completed Oct 24, 1861; closure announced Oct 26, 1861 (two days later) - accurate.

E035-10.notes: Only A addresses why it is remembered despite short life. Fact check: April 1860 to Oct 1861 is about eighteen months; accurate. B, C, D are off-goal details (D's eight states is accurate; C's wage figure commonly cited).
